sections.text_helper: Section 49.2.7 "OEMKEY and BSKEY password management" in chapter 49 (Debug support (DBG)), RM0522 Rev 1, page 2417.
sections.section_content:
Readout protection (RDP) L2 and L2_wBS can be changed to L0 under the condition that
a128-bit OEMKEY was provisioned under RDP L0. That is an RDP regression.
Read-out protection L2_wBS can be changed to L2 thanks to the BSKEY. This is an RDP
transition.
[Figure 744. Product life cycle states and regression management]
Regression request
OEMKEY Yes
password Regression
match
RDP L0
Figure744 shows the product life cycle and regression mechanism. If the device is
inRDP_STATE “L2” or “L2_BS”, the debug state is CLOSED. The regression procedure
allows a full-regression if the adequate password (128-bit OEMKEY) is provided under reset
to the DBGMCU_DBG_AUTH_HOST register, thanks to JTAG or SWD.
RDP regression erases the entire user flash memory area.
OEMKEY regression principle
The RDP regression protocol is based on a password (OEMKEY) provisioned under
RDP_L0 to trigger the full regression action. The OEMKEY must be provisioned under
RDPL0. After option-byte loading, the OEMLOCK bit in FLASH_SR indicates if an
OEMKEY has been provisioned. If reset, no OEMKEY is provisioned under RDP L0, and
theregression is impossible.
The host can write this password to the DBGMCU_DBG_AUTH_HOST register via the
JTAG/SWD interface. It can get information on product identification through
theDBGMCU_DBG_AUTH_DEVICE register.
If the provided password matches the populated key, the regression is automatically started
by hardware.
OEMKEY validation principle
The OEMKEY password is write only. Transitioning to RDP L2 or L2_wBS with an incorrect
password loaded, means that it becomes impossible for the user to regress to RDP L0.
Inorder to verify OEMKEY under RDP L0 prior transitioning to RDP L2 or RDP L2_wBS, a
validation mechanism exists.
To validate the OEMKEY the host can write the password in DBGMCU_DBG_AUTH_HOST
via the JTAG/SWD interface under reset and RDP L0.
Once the provided password has been compared to the OEMKEY, the VAL_RDY status flag
is set in DBGMCU_DBG_VALR. The VAL_OEMKEY bit indicates then if the OEMKEY
password provided for validation matches the provisioned one.
BSKEY transition principle
The RDP transition protocol to go from RDP L2_wBS to RDP_L2 (to close the boundary
scan) is based on a password (BSKEY) populated under RDP_L0 to trigger the full
regression action. A default value (0xAAAAAAAA) is preloaded during manufacturing.
The host can write this password to DBGMCU_BSKEY_HOST via the JTAG/SWD interface.
It can get information on product identification through DBGMCU_DBG_AUTH_DEVICE.
If the provided password matches the provisioned key, the transition is automatically started
by hardware.
Figure745 shows the product life cycle states during a transition stage from RDP L2_wBS
to L2. The debug state is CLOSED in both of these product lifecycles.
